fact: The GIA revealed the draft national policy for open government data on 27 November 2025, with a national technical guide issued, and said it would distribute both to government entities for official adoption.

The GIA, which runs the platform, launched the Open Government Data Platform at opendata.gia.gov.ly on 27 November 2025, simultaneously with the draft national open data policy, with first-phase datasets, APIs and indicators but no dataset count or named publishing bodies.

The GIA, which runs the platform at opendata.gia.gov.ly, reported statistics to February 2026 of 91 datasets, 9 active government entities participating and 8 sectors covered; the document does not tie the platform to an open data policy.

The General Information Authority met sectoral information centres, ministries and outside experts on 14 October 2026 to fold a national survey's results into the final draft of a National Policy for Open Data and Artificial Intelligence, which is still being completed.
